clue.text: Empty box with shell-like lining

indicators.note: the shell-like forms a lining inside the word for box, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: to box someone is to hit them, a clout
shell-like is crosswordese (and British slang) for an ear, from its shape

explanation.surface: A packing case is emptied, revealing an inner lining patterned like a seashell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' looks like a noun (a carton) but is the verb to hit. 'Shell-like' as a noun is British slang for an ear ('a word in your shell-like').
explanation.definitionFit: To clear something out is to remove all its contents, leaving it bare.

clue.text: Rummage through business storage unit

parts.note: Co. is short for company, a business
MB, a megabyte, is a unit of computer storage

explanation.surface: Someone searches a company's warehouse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Storage unit' suggests a warehouse; it is the computing unit MB.
explanation.definitionFit: To comb a place is to search it thoroughly.

clue.text: Does it contribute to rising Sicilian terror?

definitions.text: Does it contribute to rising Sicilian terror?

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
the words Sicilian terror each contribute some letters to the run within them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about what feeds the fear felt in Sicily.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Does it contribute' as the definition, which does not define a volcano; the whole clue is the definition, a Sicilian terror. In a down clue 'rising' reads ANTE upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is Sicily's active volcano, whose eruptions have terrified islanders for centuries.

clue.text: It is flowery to wearers

indicators.note: flowery, as in florid, ornate, signals the letters being dressed up in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A perfume smells of blossom to those who put it on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flowery' does double duty as description and anagram signal, so the whole clue is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rosewater is a fragrant liquid distilled from petals, worn as a scent.

clue.text: Without control, came down after turbulence

indicators.note: after means the word for came down follows the word for turbulence

parts.note: turbulence, social upheaval, is unrest
rain came down, it rained

explanation.surface: Rain poured uncontrollably after a bumpy spell of weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turbulence' suggests weather; it is political unrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrestrained means unchecked, free of any restriction.

clue.text: In-your-face depravity reduced at each fringe theatre

indicators.note: the joined words for in-your-face and depravity are trimmed at both edges, losing their first and last letters

parts.note: in-your-face behaviour is brazen, bold
depravity is vice, moral corruption

explanation.surface: A critic sneers that a fringe theatre's shocking, decadent show has been toned down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fringe theatre' looks like one phrase, but 'fringe' belongs to the indicator. The OLD VIC is a historic London theatre near Waterloo.
explanation.definitionFit: A well-known London playhouse, an example of a theatre.

clue.text: One occupying teaching department in France

indicators.note: occupying means the letter for one sits inside the word for teaching

parts.note: lore is traditional teaching or knowledge
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single person staffs a French school's teaching department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teaching department' looks like a school unit, but 'department in France' is the definition: Loire is one of France's administrative départements.
explanation.definitionFit: Loire is an administrative region of France, named after its longest river.

clue.text: Cases secure with damages

indicators.note: cases secure (hold fast) another word inside them

parts.note: valises are travelling cases
and means with, in addition to

explanation.surface: Lockable suitcases come with breakages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Damages' looks like a noun (compensation); it is the verb, wrecks.
explanation.definitionFit: To vandalise is to deliberately wreck or deface property.

clue.text: One sees picture blurred once image runs

indicators.note: a blurred image has its parts smeared together, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Someone watches a photo go fuzzy after the colours run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture' means a film (going to the pictures), so the one who sees it is a filmgoer.
explanation.definitionFit: A cinemagoer watches films, which the British call pictures.

clue.text: The clergy's wickedness I'm about to experience

indicators.note: about turns round the words for wickedness and I'm together, so they are read backwards

parts.note: wickedness is sin
I'm taken as its letters, the apostrophe dropped
to experience something is to try it

explanation.surface: Someone confesses they are about to find out how wicked the priesthood can be.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'clergy' is a link meaning is. 'About' turns the two words together, so I'm comes out in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of priests and pastors in a church is collectively called its ministry.

clue.text: One who really likes eating local fish

indicators.note: eating means the word for an enthusiast takes in the word for local, wrapping round it

parts.note: someone who really likes a thing is a fan of it
a local is a British pub, an inn

explanation.surface: A keen diner tucks into fish caught nearby.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain 'the local' is one's neighbourhood pub, here INN. Finnan haddock is a Scottish smoked haddock, named after Findon near Aberdeen.
explanation.definitionFit: Finnan is smoked haddock, a type of fish.

clue.text: Desert ship after offering intelligence on hard old fighter

indicators.note: on means one piece is placed on top of the next in this down clue
after means the desert ship follows the other pieces

parts.note: a sop is an offering made to placate someone
wit is intelligence, good sense
H is the pencil-grading abbreviation for hard
the camel is called the ship of the desert

explanation.surface: A camel is offered information about a tough old warrior.
explanation.walkthrough: The Sopwith Camel was a British fighter plane of World War I.
explanation.definitionFit: A biplane fighter of the First World War, now long retired.

clue.text: Press reluctant person thus to compose a sermon

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer tells you to twist (rearrange) the letters of its last two words, which composes the two words a sermon

explanation.surface: A vicar leans on an unwilling helper to get a sermon written.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer read literally is a recipe: TWIST, an anagram signal, followed by ONES ARM, whose letters rearranged spell A SERMON. 'Thus to compose' points to the answer as that recipe.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to pressure or coerce someone unwilling into doing something.

clue.text: Like baby food, fresh-wrapped

indicators.note: the word for fresh is wrapped round the word for food, enclosing it

parts.note: a fresh day is cool, chilly
a dish is a serving of food

explanation.surface: Baby food is sold freshly packaged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh-wrapped' looks like one packaging term; 'fresh' gives CHILLY and 'wrapped' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting childishly is behaving immaturely, as an infant would.

clue.text: Scrap copper collected by moto sport bodies

parts.note: Formula One motor racing is F1, written FI with the numeral as a letter

indicators.note: the metal is collected by, so held inside, the other words

parts.note: stiffs is slang for corpses, dead bodies
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: Scrap metal is gathered up by racing authorities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap copper' reads as junk metal, but 'scrap' is a fight and 'copper' is CU, not a policeman. 'Bodies' suggests organisations; it is STIFFS, corpses.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight, and fisticuffs is fighting with fists.

clue.text: Jack is buried by 20

indicators.note: the word is goes inside the word supplied by 20, buried in it

parts.note: the answer to 20 across means glowing with heat, so hot

explanation.surface: A sailor named Jack lies in a grave dug by someone numbered twenty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a name; it is the verb to jack up, lift. The cross-reference 20 means its answer (white-hot), giving HOT.
explanation.definitionFit: To jack a car up is to raise it, as a winch or crane would lift a load.

clue.text: On return stroke, perhaps the greatest adjustment

parts.note: re means on or concerning, as in a letter heading

indicators.note: return means the word for stroke is turned back and read the other way

parts.note: a stroke of the oar is a row
a king is the greatest of his realm, one example of a supreme figure

explanation.surface: A tennis player's backhand return, possibly the best ever, was a modified shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Return stroke' reads as one tennis phrase, but 'return' reverses ROW to WOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A reworking is a revision or alteration of something already made.

clue.text: Mysterious figure said to have mysterious diet

indicators.note: said means the word for figure is spoken, and we take letters matching how it is heard

parts.note: to figure is to reckon or estimate

indicators.note: mysterious suggests the letters of diet are puzzlingly disordered

explanation.surface: An enigmatic person is rumoured to follow a strange eating plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' looks like a person; it is the verb to reckon. 'Mysterious' appears twice: first the definition, then the anagram signal for DIET.
explanation.definitionFit: Recondite means obscure, little known and hard to understand.

clue.text: Misspelt URL — it's the main idea of service provider

indicators.note: something misspelt has its letters out of order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: only it is used; the 's is a link meaning is
the gist is the main idea or essence

explanation.surface: Someone complains that a web address typed wrongly is the whole point of an internet service provider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Service provider' suggests an internet company; here it is one who leads a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: A liturgist compiles or conducts the forms of public worship, providing a church service.

clue.text: Found a lost island of the Minoans

indicators.note: lost means a letter given in the clue goes missing from the word

parts.note: to found something is to create it

explanation.surface: An archaeologist reports discovering a vanished island of the ancient Minoan people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Found' looks like the past of 'find'; it is the verb to establish. 'A lost' tells you an A goes from CREATE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Minoan civilisation of the Bronze Age was centred on this Greek island, home of Knossos.

clue.text: Dazzling fall of ancient civilization

parts.note: Incan describes something of the Inca, an ancient civilisation of the Andes
a fall is a descent

explanation.surface: A historian describes the spectacular collapse of an old empire.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says 'fall of' the civilisation, but the answer puts INCAN (of the Inca) first, then DESCENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something glowing white-hot is brilliantly bright, so dazzling.

clue.text: Name that is given to extremely close relative

parts.note: i.e. is short for id est, that is

indicators.note: extremely takes the letters at the extremes of close, its first and last

explanation.surface: A family name is passed down to a very near kin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely close relative' looks like a phrase, but 'extremely' picks the first and last letters of 'close'.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a sibling's daughter, a family relation.

clue.text: One wet place turned into very dry one

indicators.note: turned means the words for one and a wet place are turned round together, read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
a bog is wet, marshy ground

explanation.surface: A marsh dried out and became an arid desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gobi is a desert in Mongolia and China.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gobi is a vast arid desert in Asia.

clue.text: Five-one to Germany — that shows style

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral five
ein is the German word for one

explanation.surface: A football score of five-one to Germany demonstrates their flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Five-one' reads as a match score; it is V, then 'one' as a German would say it.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak in a humorous vein is to use that manner or style.

clue.text: Thought about paper, felt its weight

indicators.note: about means the word for thought goes round the word for paper, enclosing it

parts.note: heed is thought or attention, as in 'gave no heed'
FT is the Financial Times, a British newspaper

explanation.surface: Someone reflected on a document and sensed how weighty it was.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thought' looks like a verb but is the noun HEED.
explanation.definitionFit: To heft something is to lift it to judge how heavy it is.

clue.text: Room 23 reserved for unfussy diner

indicators.note: re-served, served again in a new way, so the letters are dished up in a different order

parts.note: 23 stands for the answer to 23 down, a blood vessel

explanation.surface: A hotel room numbered 23 has been booked for a guest who eats anything.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserved' looks like 'booked' but splits as re-served, served up again in a new order. The 23 is a cross-reference to another answer in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: An omnivore eats both plants and meat, so will eat almost anything.

clue.text: People with no fear?

parts.note: read not as fearless people but as people who fear the word no, never daring to refuse

explanation.definitionFit: Toadies who always agree with superiors, too timid ever to refuse them.

clue.text: North African brew restricts good rain supply

indicators.note: restricts means the word for brew hems in the letter for good

parts.note: a brew here is beer, ale

indicators.note: supply read as the adverb of supple, flexibly, so the next word bends into a new order

explanation.surface: A drink from North Africa holds back a decent water supply.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the noun; it is the adverb (supplely), an anagram signal for RAIN, giving RIAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An Algerian is a person from Algeria, a country of North Africa.
